text:
elaine: Heads up — SOC2 request: we need concrete audit evidence of KMS usage across AWS/GCP/Azure for envelope encryption and key rotation. Who owns collection/queries?

samir: I can start. Do we need both Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey events?

elaine: Yes — for envelope encryption we need GenerateDataKey (or GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext) on AWS, and the equivalent Encrypt/Decrypt+Asymmetric operations on GCP/Azure. Also show which CMK/KeyVault key id was used.

maya: Quick note: AWS CloudTrail records Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey* events. For GCP, look at "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Encrypt" / "Decrypt" in Audit Logs. For Azure Key Vault, Diagnostic logs include AuditEvent with Operations like "encrypt" and "unwrapKey".

adrian: Pasting the commands I usually run for evidence collection:
```
# AWS (query CloudTrail S3 or LookupEvents)
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GenerateDataKey --start-time 2024-09-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-09-30T23:59:59Z
# or if using S3 CloudTrail logs + Athena: filter eventName IN ('GenerateDataKey','GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext','Encrypt','Decrypt') and extract requestParameters.ciphertextBlob and kmsKeyId

# GCP (Cloud Logging)
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt"' --project=my-project --limit=500

# Azure (Log Analytics)
// in Logs: AzureDiagnostics | where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT" and OperationName startswith "Encrypt"
```

kate: For rotation evidence: AWS CMK has key rotation flag and key versions for AWS CloudHSM customers; you can fetch key metadata: `aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key>` and `aws kms list-keys` with DescribeKey. For GCP, check KeyRing.CryptoKeyVersion state and creationTime. For Azure, list key versions under Key Vault and diagnostic events showing "update"/"create" operations.

elaine: Good. We also need mapping between application-level ops (GenerateDataKey used by envelope encryption) and the higher-level API calls in our runtime. Samir, Maya: can you annotate a small sample of logs pointing to which app request used which key (include request id or trace id)?

samir: On it. I'll join traces to CloudTrail events using invocation ids in the runtime logs — we emit `x-request-id` that we persist in the KV cache traces.

maya: I put a short query for GCP that helped us link a trace:
```
protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" AND jsonPayload.request.id="<runtime-request-id>"
```
It returns protoPayload.resourceName which includes the key resource (`projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*`) so you can prove which key version was used.

adrian: For packaging evidence: 1) gather raw log slices (CloudTrail/Cloud Logging/Azure Diagnostics) with timestamps + event ids, 2) include a short mapping doc that shows how request ids map to events, 3) include key metadata (describe-key output / key version list), 4) include retention policy proof (S3 bucket lifecycle or Logs retention).

kate: One gotcha: cross-account KMS usage — CloudTrail might show `arn:aws:kms:..:account-id:key/...` that belongs to another account. Make sure we include the accountId field and any AssumeRole logs to prove who initiated the call.

elaine: Also confirm retention windows for each cloud: AWS CloudTrail event history vs S3 delivery retention, GCP logs retention depends on Logging bucket (we keep 365d for audit), Azure diagnostic settings retention can be set on storage / Log Analytics. Add screenshots of retention config.

samir: Quick sample Athena snippet I use to pull useful columns:
```
SELECT eventTime, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity.accountId, requestParameters.kmsKeyId, requestParameters.ciphertextBlob, additionalEventData.ciphertextLength, json_extract_scalar(userIdentity, '$.arn') as arn
FROM cloudtrail_logs_table
WHERE eventName IN ('GenerateDataKey','GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext','Encrypt','Decrypt')
AND eventTime BETWEEN '2024-09-01' AND '2024-09-30'
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
```

maya: For Azure CLI retrieval of diag settings: `az monitor diagnostic-settings list --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>` then pull the storageAccountId or workspaceId fields. Include the JSON payload as evidence.

elaine: Nice. Can we also add a short section answering auditor Q: "How do you ensure keys used for envelope encryption are rotated and that old data remains decryptable?"

kate: Answer: we use key versioning + key rotation policy. For envelope encryption we store the key version identifier (AWS: ciphertextBlob uses key ID and key version implicitly; GCP/Azure: include CryptoKeyVersion in metadata), and our object metadata contains the wrapped key version. When rotating, new GenerateDataKey calls use new key versions; older objects retain wrapped keys referencing the old version so decryption uses the correct version. Provide a short diagram & sample object metadata in the package.

adrian: Also include a control note: restricted RBAC to keys: only service principals for runtime and ops role can call GenerateDataKey; rotation permissions limited to security-admin role. Provide IAM policy snippets.

samir: IAM snippet for AWS in case helpful:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/*","Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:CallerAccount": "123456789012"}}}
  ]
}
```

sec-audit-bot: Reminder: please attach hashes (SHA256) of the exported log bundles to the ticket and mark retention proof as redacted if copying into external evidence pack.

elaine: Thanks everyone — Samir & Maya, aim to drop raw bundles + mapping doc into the SOC2 folder by EOD tomorrow. Adrian/Kate please prepare the short writeup on rotation and RBAC. I'll compile and send to auditors. :thumbsup:

kate: ack, will prepare the writeup and IAM snippets.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline check — no RBAC infra changes detected in last 7 days.

elaine: Perfect. If anyone hits blockers, ping me directly.
